consensus_summary: Primary meaning of the great fish is God's instrument of judgment/deliverance for Jonah and especially the type of Christ's three-day burial and resurrection (the sign of Jonah explicitly from the Gospels); sea-monsters more broadly as chaos/evil powers or hostile empires (Egypt/Babylon etc.) appear only as alternatives, alongside fish as believers or ICHTHYS for Christ; no single settled meaning for the compound term.
book_summary: A devouring kingdom that swallows and is forced to give back.
consensus_core_identification: Great fish as type of Christ's burial/resurrection (sign of Jonah) or the death-realm/grave from which God delivers.
book_core_identification: Devouring kingdom that swallows and is forced to give back.
boundary_disagreement: Consensus keeps the great-fish primary as christological type (with empire readings as separate alternatives for mythic sea-monsters); book reassigns the whole term (great fish/sea-monster) to political kingdoms that devour and regurgitate, shifting the boundary away from the tomb typology.
material_contradiction: The great fish cannot have as its core sense both the type of Christ's tomb/death-realm and a devouring kingdom; accepting the book's identification replaces the consensus primary referent.
rationale: All three consensus responses fix the primary core on the Jonah great fish as the sign of Jonah (Christ's three days in the tomb) or divine instrument of death-like preservation, treating empire/chaos readings only as alternatives for sea-monsters. The book's entry instead asserts a devouring kingdom that swallows and is forced to give back (supported by its Jer/Ezek citations of Babylon/Egypt as dragon/whale). This is a replaced central identification rather than a mere boundary tweak of the same category, even though empire language appears in the listed alternatives; the book's own common-view note further confirms it sets the consensus primary aside.
strongest_objection: Matthew 12:39-40 (and parallels) explicitly authorizes the great fish as the type of the Son of Man's three days in the heart of the earth, so any kingdom reading drawn from other sea-monster texts remains secondary and cannot displace that core without contradiction.
